summary: 1921 Pennsylvania Department of Forestry steel Aermotor tower on South Mountain in Michaux State Forest; its current status is unresolved after a 2021 demolition contract.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with a glass-enclosed cab
facts.status_note: Listed in 2018, but a 2021 online contract called for demolition and a 2024 visitor found nothing to see at the site. Completion of the demolition is not confirmed.

access.note: State-owned Michaux State Forest land per a 1942 survey, reached by a road walk off the Appalachian Trail past several homes. A 2024 visitor found nothing to see at the site.

visit.trail_note: Short detour from the Appalachian Trail off Shippensburg Road; a 2024 visitor found nothing to see at the site.

corrections.why: 24.4 m is 80 ft, from Willhite's opening line. NHLR and the 1921 notice give 60 ft, which Willhite also cites as other reports' figure.
A 2021 demolition contract and a 2024 visit that found nothing to see at the site make standing doubtful. No record confirms the demolition was completed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR and the 1921 notice give 60 ft; Willhite gives 80 ft in its opening line, notes other reports say 60 ft, and records a 1942 survey of 75 ft. 18.3 m (60 ft) is used as the best-supported figure.

NHLR (2018) describes the tower as sitting on South Mountain. Willhite reports a 2021 demolition contract and a 2024 visit that found nothing at the site. The status is unknown until a completion record or current visit is found.

notes_for_editor: Current status is the main open question. The NHLR spells the forest 'Michael State Forest'; the Forest Lookouts page gives Michaux State Forest, which is used. Access level 'public' is inferred from state ownership (1942 survey) and the road-walk detour, not stated by a source. A 2024 review giving 80 ft and good condition appeared only in a search summary and was not fetched. The DCNR self-guided tour brochure gives 1921 and 60 ft, but its text was too interleaved to quote, so it is not cited. Lookout observers are named in the source; they are not named in the story. Confirm current status with the Pennsylvania Bureau of Forestry before publication.
